title: Coherent ring diagrams from upper extensions of chains
statement: theorem exists_compatible_ring_tower (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (K : Type v) [CommRing K] (I : Type w) (q : I → K) (P : ∀ (A : Type w) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A], (A →+* K) → Prop) (hbase : ∃ (A : Type w) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : Algebra R A) (ψ : A →+* K), P A ψ) (hstep : ∀ (J : Type w) [LinearOrder J] [Nonempty J] (A : J → Type w) [∀ j, CommRing (A j)] [∀ j, Algebra R (A j)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → A i →ₐ[R] A j) [DirectedSystem A (fun i j h ↦ f i j h)] (ψ : ∀ j, A j →+* K), (∀ i j h a, ψ j (f i j h a) = ψ i a) → (∀ j, P (A j) (ψ j)) → ∀ x : K, ∃ (B : Type w) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra R B) (φ : B →+* K) (g : ∀ j, A j →ₐ[R] B), (∀ i j h a, g j (f i j h a) = g i a) ∧ (∀ j a, φ (g j a) = ψ j a) ∧ P B φ ∧ ∃ b, φ b = x) : ∃ (_ : LinearOrder I) (A : I → Type w) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (A i)) (_ : ∀ i, Algebra R (A i)) (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → A i →ₐ[R] A j), DirectedSystem A (fun i j h ↦ f i j h) ∧ ∃ (ψ : ∀ i, A i →+* K), (∀ i j h a, ψ j (f i j h a) = ψ i a) ∧ (∀ i, P (A i) (ψ i)) ∧ (∀ i, ∃ a, ψ i a = q i)

source.place: fourth proof paragraph (well-ordering and coherent transfinite recursion); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03C3

proof.text: Choose a well-order on I and a base stage from hbase. Use ordinary well-founded recursion on a fixed type of records. A record stores its stage carrier, ring and R-algebra structures, its map to K, and, for every index of I, an incoming algebra map with its domain carrier and structures. At index i, test whether the earlier records form a coherent diagram: their incoming-map domains must agree with the stored earlier stages, their maps must satisfy the identity and composition laws, and their maps to K must commute. If they do, and there are predecessors, apply hstep to that diagram on the strict initial segment and x = q i. Store the resulting stage and cocone maps. If there are no predecessors, apply hstep to the singleton base diagram and x = q i. Fill unused incoming-map entries with the identity of the new stage. If the earlier records are incoherent, use the base record as a default. Fix these choices before recursing. All records form a type in universe w+1 (or larger to hold the parameters), so well-founded recursion applies without increasing any carrier's universe. By well-founded induction the default branch is never used. The cocone equations give composition with all preceding transitions and compatibility with K; identities give the diagonal maps. The domains stored in the new record are exactly the previously chosen carriers. Thus the recursively chosen records give one coherent diagram. The new stage satisfies P and contains q i by hstep. This also covers finite orders, orders with limit stages, and the empty order (where the final diagram is empty). Choices are made inside this existence proof, not used to define any ring.

mathlib_searches.query: A well ordered compatible diagram can be built by recursively extending each previous initial segment by a coherent cocone
transfinite construction of compatible directed diagrams from coherent upper bounds of nonempty chains
mathlib_searches.results: InverseSystem.limit defines compatible families; Functor.WellOrderInductionData.Extension.instNonempty and ofExists require an already given inverse functor and successor/limit lifting data. These are machinery, not a one-line specialization to variable carrier rings and incoming maps.
